prompt: You want to learn to touch-type — type without looking at the keyboard. Which practice plan is most likely to work?

options.text: Type normally while looking at the keys, but try to go faster each day
Learn the home-row finger positions, practise in short daily sessions without looking down, and accept slow, accurate typing at first
Memorise a picture of the keyboard before touching a computer
Practise for one very long session once a month

explanation: Touch typing rests on placing the fingers on the home row and building muscle memory through regular practice without looking at the keys. Accuracy first is what lets speed follow; constantly looking down prevents the finger patterns from ever becoming automatic.
